chunks: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

You should say at the time of breaking the fast until the end of every night of the month of Ramadan: 'All praise is due to Allah who enabled us, so we fasted, and provided for us, so we broke the fast. O Allah, accept from us, help us in it, keep us safe in it, and accept it from us with ease from You and well-being. And all praise is due to Allah who discharged for us one day of the month of Ramadan.'

key_terms.تَقَبَّلْ: Accept (as in accepting acts of worship)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when breaking the fast during Ramadan?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this supplication highlights the Shia emphasis on daily gratitude (shukr) and the spiritual significance of each completed day of fasting as a distinct act of worship. It reflects the scholarly tradition of viewing iftar not merely as a physical break but as a moment for seeking divine acceptance (qabul) and ease (yusr) in the completion of the religious duty.
